title: Reducing Alert Fatigue and Clear Oncall Ownership: A Customer-Facing Incident Playbook
author: Asha Murthy
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines how Redwood’s Customer Success, Support, and Platform teams should coordinate to reduce alert noise, establish unambiguous oncall ownership, and manage customer-visible incidents with minimal customer disruption. It is focused on enterprise tenants (Dedicated/Private) but also applies to hosted API incidents where customer impact is suspected.

Goals
- Reduce actionable pager noise by >=50% for customer-impacting alerts within three months of adoption.
- Ensure every alert has a single owning team and a documented remediation runbook or a suppression policy.
- Provide clear steps for customer-safe remediation and communications to minimize churn and SLA exposure.

Scope
- Included: alerts generated by Redwood control plane, tenant routing/proxy, model serving (inference failures), quota and billing anomalies, and integration connectors that impact request processing.
- Excluded: internal CI/CD job failures (owned by eng-infra) and local developer tooling alerts.

Definitions
- Noise: alerts that repeatedly fire without leading to a meaningful action within the past 30 days.
- Actionable Alert: an alert with a documented owner, severity, and a runbook that is executed at least once when it fires.
- Customer-facing Incident: an event where customer SLOs (availability/latency) are materially impacted, or billing/data integrity is at risk.

Roles & Ownership
- First Responder (Support/Platform): The oncall person who owns initial triage within 15 minutes. Responsibilities: validate, gather impact, open incident if needed, begin mitigation.
- Engineering Owner (Runtime/Infra/Product): Team responsible for full remediation and post-incident follow-up. Must be staffed for major incidents.
- Customer Success Lead (CS): Primary communicator to customer stakeholders and coordinates internal communications for ERs/SEVs.
- Incident Commander (IC): Assigned for Sev2+/Sev1 incidents. Coordinates cross-team tasks and manages escalation.

Alert Classification Matrix
(Use this table to assign ownership and expected response time)

| Category | Example alert | Owner | Response SLA | Customer impact | Auto-suppress allowed? | Severity |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Platform Availability | control-plane-400-errors > 5% over 5m | eng-platform | 5m | High | No | Sev1 |
| Model Degradation | p95_token_latency_increase > 2x baseline | eng-serving-runtime | 15m | Moderate/High | No | Sev2 |
| Tenant Quota Hit | tenant_x_rate_limit_429s > 10/min | support | 15m | Moderate | Yes (1m suppression) | Sev2 |
| Telemetry Drop | metrics-forwarder_lag > 120s | eng-infra | 30m | Low/Moderate | Yes (grouped) | Sev3 |
| Billing Anomaly | invoice_delta > $5k unexpected | finance-legal & support | 60m | High (customer) | No | Sev1 |

Triage & Escalation Procedure (first 30 minutes)
1. First Responder acknowledges alert within Response SLA.
2. Determine if alert is symptomatic or root: check runbook tags: symptomatic -> follow immediate mitigations; root -> route to Engineering Owner.
3. If multiple alerts correlate (same tenant or upstream), mark incident and assign IC.
4. IC coordinates: set incident priority, notify CS Lead, open incident bridge, document initial timeline.
5. If customer-visible, CS Lead drafts initial comms template (internal + external) and posts a holding message to the customer’s designated channel within 30 minutes of incident start.

Runbook Patterns (examples)
- Symptomatic mitigation (fast path):
  - Example: tenant_x_rate_limit_429s
    - Action: enable short suppression (1m) for duplicate alerts; find offending tenant key; apply temporary burst-limit increase for that tenant via admin API:
      - curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/{tenant}/burst-adjust 
        -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
        -d '{"burst_window": 60, "max_burst": 500}'
    - Verify: run `curl https://telemetry.redwood/api/tenant/{tenant}/metrics | jq .rates` and ensure 429s drop below threshold for 5 consecutive minutes.

- Root cause engagement (slow path):
  - Example: p95_token_latency_increase > 2x baseline
    - Action: collect traces (tracer query examples below), review recent deployments, check GPU health and KV cache hit rate.
    - PromQL snippet to attach with incident: `increase(request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="runtime",quantile="0.95"}[5m])`
    - Escalate to eng-serving-runtime and provide packet of: tenant list, timestamps, top traces, and pre/post deploy diffs.

Alert Reduction Playbook (how to reduce noise)
1. Ownership mapping: every alert must have the `owner_team` label and a single Slack/Pager contact. No alert without owner is considered noise.
2. Suppress identical alerts for the same tenant for a configurable debounce window (default 1 minute) unless it evidences growing error rates.
3. Dedup & group by root cause: implement correlation rules in the alert router (grouping-key: tenant|service|error-code).
4. Use adaptive thresholds based on rolling windows and baseline seasonality instead of static fixed thresholds.
5. Implement an alert lifecycle: open -> acknowledged -> resolved -> closed. Alerts that bounce back without remediation are automatically escalated to IC.
6. Maintain a suppression whitelist for noisy 3rd-party integrations with documented mitigation steps.

Key Metrics to Track
- Pager burn rate: number of paged alerts per oncall shift (target < 8 actionable pages/shift).
- Alert to incident conversion: percent of alerts that become incidents (target < 10%).
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to remediate (MTTR) by alert class.
- Noise ratio: alerts suppressed / total alerts (target > 30% but balanced).
- Customer-impacting incidents per quarter (trend must be non-increasing).

Customer Communication Templates
- Holding message (30m):
  - Subject: We’re investigating a service disruption affecting {tenant-name}
  - Body: We are aware of increased errors for your requests and our teams are investigating. We will provide an update within 1 hour. Reference: {incident-link}
- Update cadence: 30m until root cause identified, 60m after that while in mitigation, then hourly as needed.
- Post-incident summary: include timeline, root cause, customer impact (tokens/requests affected), remediation steps taken, and scheduled follow-ups.

Escalation Matrix (customer-impacting)
- Sev1 (platform down for tenant or billing integrity risk): escalate to IC, eng-platform lead, CS Director, and Legal/Finance on call. Pager -> immediate bridge.
- Sev2 (degraded inference quality/latency impacting SLAs): Support first responder -> eng-serving-runtime -> CS Lead -> scheduled customer update.
- Sev3 (telemetry or low-impact errors): owner team handles within standard SLAs; escalate on repeated bounce.

Implementation Checklist (for Support & Platform)
- [ ] Annotate all alerts with owner_team, severity, and runbook link.
- [ ] Configure the alert router: suppression windows, grouping keys, and dedupe rules.
- [ ] Add Slack channel / PagerDuty escalation bindings per team.
- [ ] Create customer comms templates and CS contact list per enterprise tenant.
- [ ] Create dashboards: Alert noise panel, top firing rules, MTTA/MTTR trends, per-tenant alert volume.

Sample Alert Definitions (examples for runtime engineers)
- p95 latency spike (Prometheus):
  - ALERT RuntimeHighP95Latency
  - IF histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance)) > 2.0
  - FOR 3m
  - LABELS { severity="page", owner_team="eng-serving-runtime" }

- Tenant error rate (example rule):
  - ALERT TenantHighErrorRate
  - IF increase(http_requests_total{status=~"5..",tenant=~".+"}[5m]) / increase(http_requests_total[5m]) > 0.05
  - LABELS { severity="page", owner_team="support" }

Oncall Handover & Fatigue Reduction Practices
- Handover notes: outgoing oncall must leave the top 3 active alerts, any muted rules, and follow-ups in the team Handoff doc.
- Scheduled quiet windows: non-urgent noisy alerts may be auto-muted during scheduled low-traffic maintenance windows if documented and approved by CS.
- Rotation length: prefer 7-day rotations for platform teams and 3-4 day rotations for support to balance knowledge and burnout. Review quarterly.
- Pager triage cap: any engineer receiving >12 pages in a day must have their load reviewed by manager; consider temporary rotation pause.

Post-Incident & Continuous Improvement
- Post-Incident Tasks (within 72 hours):
  1. Full RCA and timeline (eng owner).
  2. Action items assigned with owner and due date.
  3. Alert audit: any alert that fired and did not lead to remediation must be suppressed or reclassified.
  4. Customer-facing summary drafted and approved by CS Lead and Legal (if PII/financial impact).
- Quarterly Alert Review: each team publishes an alert inventory and noise metrics; operations council reviews and approves suppression/threshold changes.

Playbook for Customer-Facing Degraded Performance (quick checklist)
1. Validate incident and measure customer impact (requests, latency, error rate).
2. If impact confirmed, IC open and CS Lead notified.
3. Apply symptomatic mitigations (traffic shaping, fallback models, tenant routing to warm capacity).
4. If mitigation succeeds, prepare customer rollback and update comms.
5. If mitigation fails, escalate to engineering and determine rollback or multi-tenant fallback.

Appendices
A. Useful Queries and Tools
- Traces: `trace-search --tenant {tenant} --from {iso-ts} --to {iso-ts}`
- Top error sample: `curl https://telemetry.redwood/api/errors?tenant={t}&window=10m | jq .top`
- Alert router health check: `kubectl -n observability exec router-0 -- /bin/healthcheck`

B. Contacts
- Support Pager: #support-pager (Slack) and PagerDuty escalation policy: Redwood-Support-Escalation
- Eng Platform oncall: eng-platform-oncall@redwood.internal
- CS Director: cs-director@redwood.internal

C. Change History
- 2026-03-01: Created by Asha Murthy (published).
- 2026-06-10: Added sample PromQL and tenant mitigation API examples (reviewer: Benji Park).
- 2026-10-12: Expanded metrics section and added rotation guidance (reviewer: Lena Hoffmann).

If you are implementing these changes, coordinate with Observability (eng-platform) and Support for a staged rollout. For assistance, tag @cs-ops in #ops-requests.
